kind: second-pass council on the council fixes (0e996b6..c26799c): two read-only reviewers (R1 false closure/opening, R2 order/determinism/records/cost), each P0/P1 adversarially verified

reviewers.summary:
Reviewer R1 checked whether the council fixes (65f0681, 41d6395, 2e607ad) can falsely close or falsely open a space. I read the code only and ran nothing; the results below are traced on pixel fixtures in the style of compound-facade.test.ts (20 px/m, WALL=12, facade grid line y=280).

**Main defect (P0, R1).** glazingAlone, the A1/B2 fix, refuses a real glazed back between two returns whenever any row of the recess floor between t and depth−t holds 70% or more ink. It does not ask whether that row is continuous, so a dashed outline of the floor or roof above counts. At 0e996b6 such a line read DASHED and was ignored, and the glazed back was found. Now:
- no recess is detected and no back-wall grid line is added;
- if a callout is printed at the mouth, the callout rule shuts the mouth, because the returns run on as interior walls past 4.5 m. The recess becomes BUILT (R2: the B1/C1 depth premise does not prove that no back wall was missed);
- with no callout, the pocket test sees the recess and the room behind it as one cell column. Either the hall falls OUTSIDE or the recess is BUILT, depending on area.

**Sharers joint test (P1, R3).** Whether a mouth is a sharer is decided by a strict `>` on round6'd m² differences. When a mouth leads only to its own pocket, `all − leaveOneOut` equals `own` exactly in cells, but round6 and summation order can make it 1e-6 larger. With three or more undecided siblings, that sweeps a carport or porch mouth into a joint shut, and the result depends on orientation. Fix: compare integer cell counts.

**Snapshot and gaps with no separator (P2, R4).** The A2 snapshot is applied to every undecided gap, not only compound siblings. A plan with no accepted separator can therefore get a different decision from the incumbent (B shut in rotated orientations before, open now). The change removes a double-count false closure, so it errs on the safe side, but it breaks the "exactly the incumbent" contract and is not disclosed.

**Other P2/P3:**
- neighbourGlazed has no width limit and no stop-at-far-jamb check. A continuous double-line kerb or railing is excused (R6). Kosaćce's single or dashed line is not reopened, because the excuse needs this mouth to be GLAZING.
- The callout rule refuses ordinary garages whose side wall has a window or door within 4.5 m (R7).
- The joint limit uses Σ interval widths, not the merged span, so the claim that it "never shuts more than the incumbent" is false (R5).
- Whole-span records now consume COMPOUND_BOUNDS.spans. This is the only way they can change a decision (R8).
- Debug console.log lines are left in a test (R9).

**No defect found in these areas:**
- The pocket loop and the joint test have no order dependence apart from R3's float noise. The decided snapshot and ownPocket are computed before any mutation, and each group is weighed against the snapshot.
- Floods per plan rise from N to about N + Σ(|group| + 2), roughly 3N at most, which is linear and not a blow-up. glazingAlone exits early and is bounded by backWallReads.
- RECESS_MOUTH siblings are correctly kept out of joint groups.
- Spans with no accepted separator add no structural evidence.

findings.title: glazingAlone refuses a real glazed back on any dashed overhead line across the recess floor: no recess, no back-wall grid line, so the recess is BUILT or the room behind is OPEN (regression vs 0e996b6)
findings.claim: drawnAcross(k) counts raw ink (≥ minInfill·width), not continuous strokes. Every row k∈[t, depth−t] in front of the candidate glazing must be clear, and so must rows depth+t/2+2..depth+1.5t behind it. Plans very often draw a dashed outline of the floor or roof above across a recessed entrance or terrace; at ≥70% ink it now vetoes the real glazed back at every depth. Before the fix, gapStrokes classed that dashed line as non-continuous, so the signature was DASHED, it was not taken as a back wall, and the scan went on to the glazing at its real depth. A step line, interior dimension line, mat or tile hatch in front vetoes it the same way, as does a dimension or furniture line just behind the glazing. A back wall read only as glazing between two return cross-sections (a full-width HS/sliding door at the back of a recessed terrace or loggia) is exactly the case glazingAlone exists to accept.
findings.failureScenario:
Fixture: `p = house(); p.clear(120, FRONT, 251, 279); returnAt(p,108,150); returnAt(p,180,150); p.line(120,231,179,231).line(120,236,179,236)` (glazed back, no wall stretch); `wallH(p,108,263,150); returnAt(p,252,150); doorH(p,210,225,150); vehicleDoor(p,192,251)`; then a dashed overhead line `for (let x=120; x<180; x+=8) p.line(x,250,x+5,250)` (≈80% ink, 8 runs).

Trace on the new code: at d=42 (at=238) the strokes at rows 231 and 236 read GLAZING. glazingAlone(d=42) scans rows 268..250, hits the dashed row 250 and returns false; every deeper read fails the same way, so backWallOf returns null. The interval is not a recess and no Y line is added at ≈233.5. The mouth is BLANK, so the interval is OPEN_SIDE. The pocket is the single cell column 150..280 × 120..180 (about 19 m², under the 22.5 m² limit), so it stays open and the hall falls OUTSIDE.
- Expected: classAt(150,255)==='RECESS' and builtAt(150,200)===true.
- Predicted: builtAt(150,200)===false.
- With a hall deep enough to exceed the limit, the interval is shut instead and classAt(150,255) becomes BUILT.
- At 0e996b6, d=24..30 reads DASHED (not covered) and d=42 reads GLAZING (covered), so the recess is found, the line is added, and the outcome is correct.
findings.proposedFix: In glazingAlone, count a row as drawn across only if it is one continuous line (runs ≤ 2 over [a,b], the same test gapStrokes calls `continuous`), so dashed or dotted line work never vetoes. To refuse flights and patterns without refusing a single step: veto in front only when two or more separate continuous lines lie there, or when one lies within 1.5t of the candidate. Keep the behind check. Add the fixture above, plus a single-step variant, across all TRANSFORMS.

findings.title: Callout depth rule (B1/C1 fix) still shuts a recess whose returns run on as interior walls past an unread back wall
findings.claim: The rule's premise is that walls running deeper than RECESS_MAX_DEPTH_M on both sides mean no set-back wall was missed. That does not follow. A recess or loggia's side walls very often continue as partitions of the rooms behind (T-junction at the back), so left/right ≥ 4.5 m holds even when a back wall exists and backWallOf did not read it. R1 shows the back is now refused more often. calloutsOf binds callouts within max(4t, 1.5 m) of the facade line, so the callout of the back glazing or door of a 1–2 m deep recess binds at the mouth. That is C1's original scenario.
findings.failureScenario: Take the R1 fixture and add `callouts=[{id:'c',at:{x:150,y:292},widthsCm:[{value:300,confidence:0.9}]}]`. The returns at 108 and 180 run to row 150 (6.5 m ≥ 4.5 m), the right bound is a SEPARATOR, jambInk is [true,true], and the 300 cm callout matches the 3.0 m mouth. The interval becomes OPENING_IN_WALL, the recess cells (150,255) become BUILT, and the hall merges with them. Expected: classAt(150,255)==='RECESS'. At 0e996b6 this was a RECESS_MOUTH, because the glazed back was found first.
findings.proposedFix: Let the callout close a mouth only when backWallOf, re-run without its veto filters, also sees no drawn-across glazing or leaf between the returns at any depth ≤ RECESS_MAX_DEPTH_M. Alternatively, require that no wall-thick ink crosses between the two walls within 4.5 m and that the callout's position lies within a wall's thickness of the facade line. Add the fixture above as a mutation-gated test.

findings.title: Joint sharers test uses a strict float comparison on round6'd areas: a mouth that leads only to its own pocket can be marked a sharer and shut, and the outcome depends on orientation
findings.claim: For a mouth g that leads only to its own pocket P, the cells give all − pocketOf(group∖g) = P = own(g) exactly. In m², each term is round6(px·mppX·mppY): px is summed over cells in iy/ix order from round6'd line px, so it is not exact in binary, and round6 is applied to each term separately. Their difference can exceed own(g) by 1e-6, so `>` holds. The summation order changes under rotation or mirroring, so the misclassification is also orientation-dependent, which breaks §31.
findings.proposedFix: Decide sharers on integer cell counts, which are exact: `all.cells - pocketOf(rest).cells > ownPocket.get(g).cells`. Or compare cell sets. Compute sharedM2 from the cell set difference rather than by subtracting rounded m².

findings.title: The A2 snapshot changes decisions for gaps with no accepted separator, against the 'exactly as the incumbent' contract
findings.claim: The snapshot `decided` and the precomputed ownPocket apply to every undecided gap, compound or not. At 5957e3a and 0e996b6, a non-compound gap B was weighed against openings shut earlier in the same loop, which counted gap A's pocket twice. Now it is not. The change runs in the safe direction (it removes a false closure that depended on order), but it means a plan with no compound span no longer decides exactly as the incumbent did. The resolution only mentions A05, which is compound.
findings.failureScenario:
Fixture with no separators:
- `house()`; front gap A `clear(60,FRONT,125,279)` (3.3 m) into a hall 3.7 × 8.4 m (31 m², over its 27.2 m² limit);
- right-facade gap B `clear(348,150,359,219)` (3.5 m) into a 1.8 × 3.5 m porch (6.3 m², limit 30.6 m²).

Incumbent:
- with X lines first (identity), B is weighed before A, so B stays open;
- rotated so A is enumerated first, A is shut, then B sees 31 + 6.3 m² and is shut, and the porch becomes BUILT.

New code: B stays open in every orientation, so the decision changed for gaps with no separator.
findings.proposedFix: Either confine the snapshot and ownPocket to compound siblings and keep the incumbent's in-loop update for every other gap, or adopt the global change on purpose. If adopted, record it in the stage report and contract, and check the development matrix for changed decisions on non-compound gaps. A principled replacement is the marginal pocket computed against the current decided set, iterated to a fixpoint: it is monotone, so order-independent, and never double-counts.

findings.title: neighbourGlazed has no width or stop check: a continuous double line along the facade excuses itself through the next gap
findings.claim: neighbourGlazed accepts any next gap on the facade line whose strokes read GLAZING. It has no ≤ maxOpeningM bound and does not check that the neighbour's lines stop at its own far jamb. Two continuous thin lines inside the wall band that run across a pier (a kerb or slab edge drawn double, a terrace railing) read GLAZING in this mouth and in the next gap. jambLo/jambHi then become null and runsPast is skipped: exactly the line-runs-past signal the Kosaćce fix relies on. A single or dashed line is still not excused, so Kosaćce itself is not reopened.
findings.failureScenario: Facade: [jamb pier 1 m] [interval 3 m, open carport behind 6 m deep] [return] [recess]. Beyond the jamb pier is a 5 m open terrace gap. Two continuous lines at FRONT+3 and FRONT+8 run from x=40 through every gap and pier (railing). The interval reads GLAZING, and neighbourGlazed(lp,'LEFT') is true because the 5 m terrace gap also reads GLAZING. runsPast is skipped, so the infill rule gives OPENING_IN_WALL and the carport becomes BUILT. At 0e996b6 runsPast was true, giving OPEN_SIDE.
findings.proposedFix: Require the neighbour gap to be no wider than maxOpeningM. Also require its glazing to stop at its far jamb: run runsPast on the neighbour with its far piece's outer end as the jamb limit, or call gapStrokes with leftEnds/rightEnds on the far side.

findings.title: Callout depth rule refuses real garages whose side wall has a window or door within 4.5 m of the facade
findings.claim: left and right come from returnRun, which takes the single solid piece touching the facade. A window or door in the garage's side wall (a side window, or the door from the garage to the house) ends that piece, so the measured return can be 1.5–3 m and fail `>= deeper` (4.5 m). The callout path, 005N's main route for undrawn garage doors, is then lost for a common garage layout. With a 3 × 6.5 m garage, the pocket test leaves the garage open (19.5 m² < 22.5).
findings.failureScenario: Run test 11 (`entranceAndGarage({garage:'BLANK'})` with callout c-garage) and add a window in the garage's right wall: `p.clear(252,200,263,239)` plus two glazing lines. jambReturn(c.to+t/2) now reaches only row 240 (≈2 m), below 90 px, so the callout is refused, the interval is OPEN_SIDE and the pocket stays open. Expected: builtAt(222,210)===true. Predicted: false. At 0e996b6 it was true.
findings.proposedFix: Measure each wall's reach as the chain of solid pieces bridged across door- or window-sized holes (holes ≤ maxOpeningM that have jambs) rather than the first piece alone. Or, when either wall is shorter than 4.5 m, run backWallOf to RECESS_MAX_DEPTH_M with the longer wall's reach and accept the callout if no back wall is seen there.

findings.title: Joint limit uses the sum of interval widths, not the merged span: the claim that it 'never shuts more than the incumbent' is false
findings.claim: limitM2 = max(6, 2.5·(Σ sharer widths)²) leaves out the pier and return widths between the mouths, and any non-sharer siblings. It is therefore below the merged span's limit. Merged spans wider than maxWideOpeningM (the D1 fixture: 4 + 1 + 4 = 9 m) were never weighed by the incumbent at all. The joint test can shut what the incumbent never did. The practical risk is small (more than 160 m² enclosed behind two 4 m mouths is almost always the interior), but the stated invariant does not hold.
findings.failureScenario: Two 3 m mouths with a 1.5 m pier between them, sharing 100 m² behind. New code: 100 > 2.5·6² = 90, so both are shut. Incumbent merged 7.5 m gap: 100 ≤ 140.6, so it stays open.
findings.proposedFix: Use the merged extent (first sharer's fromPx to last sharer's toPx) for the limit, as the resolution claims, or reword the claim and record the spans over maxWideOpeningM as a deliberate extension.

findings.title: Whole-span records now consume COMPOUND_BOUNDS.spans: the only way the C2 records can change a decision
findings.claim: `if (span) spans.push(span)` now pushes spans with no intervals, and `spans.length < COMPOUND_BOUNDS.spans` counts them. On a plan with many facade gaps, a later gap that has a real separator, enumerated after 24 whole spans, is read as the incumbent would. Because X lines are enumerated before Y lines, which gap that is depends on orientation.
findings.failureScenario: A plan with 24 or more facade wide gaps holding no separator, and on a Y facade a recess-plus-garage span: identity orientation gives an uncut gap; a 90° rotation gives a cut span. This is unlikely on real sheets.
findings.proposedFix: Count only spans with intervals against the bound (`spans.filter(s => s.intervals.length > 0).length`), or keep a separate counter for cut spans.

verified.reasoning:
I could not refute the mechanism, but I rate it P1 rather than P0. I traced the code without running anything.

1. **The glazing-only branch.** In `packages/reconstruction/src/compound-facade.ts:277`, when neither piece is along the line (a glazed back drawn only between two return cross-sections), the hole counts only if the read is GLAZING and `glazingAlone(...)` is true.
2. **The veto counts raw ink.** `glazingAlone` (`compound-facade.ts:298-315`) adds up `mask.data` along each row and fails when the sum is at least `minInfill·(b−a)`. `minInfill` is 0.7 (`plan-decomposition.ts:378`). It never checks whether the ink is one continuous stroke. The front check covers every row k in [t, depth−t], and the behind check covers k in [depth+t/2+2, depth+1.5t].
3. **The claim's fixture.** Here t=12, the facade is about row 273.5, and inward is −1. The scan starts at d = max(18, 36) = 36 and steps by 6. Only d=42 (about row 231.5) holds both glazing strokes, at rows 231 and 236.
   - For d=36 the front range reaches row 250, and for d=42 it reaches row 244. The dashed line at row 250 is inside both.
   - Over x 120..179 the dashed line has dashes starting at 120, 128, …, 176, with the last one clipped. That is 46 of 60 px inked, about 77%, which is at least 0.7. So `drawnAcross` returns true and `glazingAlone` returns false.
   - The set-back wall at row 150 is deeper than RECESS_MAX_DEPTH_M (90 px), so `backWallOf` returns null.
4. **What follows.** The interval has no recess and a BLANK mouth, so it becomes OPEN_SIDE. The pocket test then decides it, with a limit of max(6, 2.5·3²) = 22.5 m². The hall plus the recess cell is about 16–19.5 m², so the mouth stays open and the hall is lost (a cell open on one side is a pocket, not built). With a deeper hall, more than 22.5 m², the mouth is shut and the recess is built.
5. **At 0e996b6.** There was no `glazingAlone`. The scan started at d=18, the dashed row read as non-continuous, and GLAZING (or a LEAF read at d=36) covered the gap, so the recess was found.
6. **Not just dashed lines.** A single solid step or threshold line in front, or any line 0.4–0.9 m behind the glazing, vetoes the same way. The docstring speaks of "line after line", but the code vetoes a single line too.

So this is a regression the B2/A1 fix introduced for a real family: a full-width glazed back between two returns. It is not a stated limit. D7/D8 in `resolution.md` cover only single stubs and glazing wider than 3.2 m.

**Why P1, not P0.**
- The failure falls back to the pocket rule, which is the normal decision for a recess whose back wall was not read.
- In the claim's own small-hall case the result is a false opening (the hall is dropped), not a false building.
- A false closure (the recess built) needs both a glazing-only back and a hall larger than the limit.
- The trigger is narrow: no stretch of back wall along the line on either side, and a line drawn in a specific 0.6 m–(depth−0.6 m) band. That is likely on some unseen houses, but it is a generic defect, not a contract break.

The proposed fix is sound: count a row only when it is one continuous stroke, and veto only on two or more continuous lines in front, or one within 1.5t of the candidate.

verified.reasoning:
The claim holds. I traced packages/reconstruction/src/plan-decomposition.ts at about lines 2068-2111.

**How pocket areas are computed.** `pocketOf` returns two things: `cells`, an exact integer, and `m2 = round6(px * mppX * mppY)`. Here `round6` is `Math.round(v*1e6)/1e6` (source-common/src/geometry.ts:43). The `px` term is a float sum of cell-size products built from round6'd line px.

**The sharers test.** It compares `all.m2 - pocketOf(rest).m2 > own(g)` strictly, with no epsilon and without using the integer `cells`.

**Why a mouth with only its own pocket can pass.** Take a mouth g whose pocket P is reachable only through g. The cell sets are then disjoint: all = P ∪ R and rest = R, so in cells the difference equals own(g) exactly. In m², though, three values are each rounded separately and then subtracted as floats. Two effects let the left side exceed own(g):
- **Separate rounding to 6 decimals.** With a = 16.5000004 and b = 150.0000004 (any non-decimal mpp gives values like these): round6(a+b) − round6(b) = 16.500000999999997, which is greater than round6(a) = 16.5. Checked with python arithmetic only.
- **Binary subtraction noise, even with clean decimals.** With 1 cm/px, a 22.2 m² carport and a 150.1 m² shared interior: all = 172.3, and 172.3 − 150.1 = 22.200000000000017 > 22.2.

**Why this becomes a false closure.**
1. Once g is wrongly in `sharers`, its width enters `widthM`, so the limit rises to 2.5·(2+2+3)² = 122.5 m².
2. `sharedM2` is about 150 m², above that limit, so every sharer, g included, becomes OPENING_IN_WALL.
3. g is now skipped in the final loop. Its own test (22.2 ≤ 22.5) would have left it open, so the carport is shut and becomes BUILT.

**Fixture (described, not run).** Same compound span; mpp 0.01 m/px.
- M1 and M2: each 2 m wide, either side of a FACADE_PIER, opening onto a 150.1 m² room that is closed on every other side.
- M3: 3 m wide, OPEN_SIDE in the same span (role ≠ RECESS_MOUTH), in front of a 3 × 7.4 m carport that is closed on its three other sides.
- Expected: M3 stays open with pocketM2 22.2. Actual: shut, with the "one of 3 mouths" why.

**Orientation dependence.** The decision turns on last-ulp and half-ulp rounding of px sums. Those sums change with iteration order and with mirrored (W − px) round6'd line positions, so §31 invariance is not guaranteed. This part is less certain than the arithmetic above, but plausible.

**Smallest fix.** Decide sharers on exact integers: `all.cells - pocketOf(rest).cells > ownPocket.get(g).cells`. Optionally compute `sharedM2` from the cell-set difference rather than by subtracting rounded m².

**Severity.** P1 rather than P0. It needs at least three undecided siblings in one span, one of them with a pocket-sized own space, and the noise falling the wrong way, roughly 1 in 8 under random fractional parts. The outcome, when it happens, is a false closure.

reviewers.summary:
Reviewer R2 (determinism, order invariance, incumbent equivalence, cost, evidence records). This was a read-only review of 0e996b6..HEAD: I ran nothing, and every scenario below is a pixel fixture still to be run.

**P0, 1 finding**
- **S1:** glazingAlone still accepts a two-line pattern between the returns' cross-sections as the set-back wall. The pattern can be a two-riser step, a linear drain or a threshold strip; some three-tread flights also pass. It reads as GLAZING, and the floor-clear and wall-behind checks have unscanned slots. A phantom room is then built in the recess: B2/A1 is not closed for 2–3 lines, and the existing fixture tests only 1 or 4.

**P1, 3 findings**
- **S2:** the A2 snapshot (weighing against openings decided before the loop) now governs every undecided gap, not only compound intervals. Plans with no accepted separator, unscaled ones included, can therefore decide differently from 5957e3a. architecture.md §3 says they keep the incumbent decision exactly, and no gate checks it. The incumbent was itself order-dependent, so "exactly the incumbent" and order invariance cannot both hold. The plain Jacobi pass also drops one cascade that was legitimate. Fix: monotone Jacobi rounds that recompute reachedOpen until nothing changes, then declare the change and diff the matrix rows.
- **S3:** whole-span records now consume COMPOUND_BOUNDS.spans (24). Before, only cut spans counted. X lines are enumerated first, so on a plan with many facade wide gaps the front's compound span can go unread in one orientation and be read when the plan is turned. The new records therefore change decisions.
- **S4:** the D1 sharer test compares differences of round6'd floating sums with a strict `>`. A mouth that leads only into its own pocket can enter the sharer set through rounding residue. It is then either shut with the group (a porch built) or it inflates the joint width and reopens a real open-plan interior.

**P2, 3 findings**
- **S5:** the D1 joint limit is not "the merged span's own limit". It uses the summed interval widths (separators excluded), with no 8 m cap. It shuts where the incumbent never could, as its own fixture shows (a 9 m merged gap). The resolution's statement "never shuts more than the incumbent did" is false.
- **S6:** compoundFacadesOf tags readings by boundary.accepted. An override built from completions alone therefore tags the outline-grid spans BOX, next to the real BOX spans, and the Evidence Pack event ids collide.
- **S7:** the callout depth rule measures only the wall piece touching the facade. A door or window in a garage's side or separator wall within 4.5 m refuses the callout, and a real blank garage with its callout stays open. This is the safe direction but generic.

**P3, 1 finding**
- **S8:** floods per plan went from 1+U to 1+U+Σ(|G|+2). Every pocket flood rebuilds wallIntervals and lineIntervals for every grid line although only the extra evidence changes. Some of the floods are exact duplicates. This is bounded, not a blow-up; caching removes most of the cost.

**Checked and clean**
- Pocket loop: grouping by spanId and the mutations inside a group are order-independent. Own pockets are precomputed against a fixed snapshot.
- Whole spans change nothing else: structuralEvidence, backWallLines and the recess cells only read accepted separators and intervals.
- D3 (more than 8 candidates leaves the gap whole) is order-independent.
- neighbourGlazed cannot reopen Kosaćce: it applies only when the mouth itself reads GLAZING.

findings.proposedFix: Smallest fix: in the cross-section/cross-section branch, extend both glazingAlone scans to cover everything outside the strokes actually counted. Front scan k∈[t, d−(half+2)], behind scan k∈[d+half+2, d+1.5t], with half = t/2. Also require the glazing strokes to be at most t·0.5 apart, which separates a pane pair from tread spacing. findings.title: The A2 snapshot changes the pocket decision of every plain gap: plans with no accepted separator (unscaled ones included) no longer decide as 5957e3a did
findings.claim: `decided` is snapshotted, and `ownPocket` is read for ALL undecided gaps, not only compound intervals. At 5957e3a and 0e996b6 the loop was sequential: a plain gap after one the loop had just shut counted that gap's pocket again. Plans with no compound span therefore change decision wherever such a cascade happened. That includes unscaled plans, where compoundOf is undefined. The resolution itself says the A05 cascade came from an unsplit 3.74 m gap. architecture.md §3 still says 'a gap with no accepted separator keeps the incumbent's decision exactly'. The unscaled-plan test only checks that no compound fields exist, not the decisions. The incumbent was itself orientation-dependent, so 'exactly the incumbent' and §31 cannot both hold. There is also a real loss: once a sibling h is shut on its own pocket, a region shared only by g and h becomes g's pocket. Jacobi never re-weighs g, so g stays open behind a wall that carries on.
findings.failureScenario: A separator-free plan: house(); the left side (an X line, enumerated first) has a 3.6 m undrawn gap into a closed 3.6 × 10.4 m hall (37 m², over its 32.4 m² limit). The front (a Y line) has a 4 m undrawn gap into a 4 × 3 m porch walled on three sides (12 m², under its 40 m² limit). At 5957e3a the hall gap is shut first, then the porch's pocket = 12 + 37 = 49 > 40, so the porch is shut and BUILT. At HEAD the porch's own pocket is 12, so it stays open. The decision changed on a plan with no accepted separator. Likewise at confidence 0 (the unscaled test's harness), where nothing compound exists.
findings.proposedFix: Replace the single Jacobi pass with monotone Jacobi rounds. Each round: recompute reachedOpen from evidence(decided), weigh every remaining undecided gap against decided ∪ {g}, apply all decisions together, and repeat until nothing changes (at most U rounds, usually 2). This stays order-invariant, never double-counts (the shut sibling's cells are no longer in reachedOpen), and restores the legitimate cascade. Then state in architecture.md and resolution.md that plain gaps' pocket decisions changed. Re-run the development matrix with a per-row diff of every non-compound wideOpenings decision against 5957e3a, and add a separator-free two-gap fixture across all TRANSFORMS.

findings.title: Whole-span records now consume the 24-span bound in enumeration order: whether a facade is read as compound depends on orientation
findings.claim: `spans.length < COMPOUND_BOUNDS.spans` counts every span pushed, and since the C2 fix that includes whole spans (intervals: []). Whole spans also include gaps wider than 8 m, because compoundOf runs before the maxWidePx check. Before 65f0681, compoundSpanOf returned null for these, so only cut spans counted. Lines are enumerated X then Y, each in ascending px. Every wide opening on a facade is usually seen on 2–3 grid lines within 1.5 walls (outer face from a chain, axis from a band). A glazed house can therefore exhaust 24 on its X-side facades before the front's Y line is reached. That front then falls back to the merged incumbent gap, while a 90° turn reads it as compound. A record-only change thus changes decisions and breaks §31.
findings.failureScenario: Draw ≥ 24 whole facade gaps on X lines. Use several >3.2 m openings with nothing in them on the left and right sides, each repeated on two or three grid lines near the side (chain ticks at outer and inner faces). Put entranceAndGarage() on the front (Y line). In 'id', spans fills with whole X spans, the front gap gets span = null, and it is decided as one merged OPEN_SIDE (recess and garage merged). In 'r90' the front becomes an X line and is read first, giving RECESS_MOUTH + OPENING_IN_WALL. At 0e996b6 the X-side gaps consumed no budget and both orientations agreed.
findings.proposedFix: Count only cut spans toward the bound: `spans.filter((s) => s.intervals.length > 0).length`. Better, make it order-free like the separator bound: collect all facade parents first, and if more than COMPOUND_BOUNDS.spans would be cut, read none and record why. Add an order test that turns a plan with many whole facade gaps.

findings.title: Sharer membership decided by `>` on differences of round6'd float areas: a mouth into its own pocket can join the group through rounding noise
findings.claim: For a mouth g whose region connects to no sibling's, the leave-one-out difference all.m2 − pocketOf(group∖g).m2 and own(g) cover the same cell set. They are computed as round6(A) − round6(B) against round6(A−B), where A and B are float sums of cell px × mppArea (and back-wall lines have non-dyadic px). The two differ by ±1e-6 or by an ulp, so `> own(g)` is true for a substantial fraction of scales. With two genuine sharers h1 and h2 in the same span, g is pulled in. Then either S > 2.5·(J+w_g)² and g, a porch, is shut with them; or g's width lifts the limit above S and the open-plan interior D1 was meant to shut stays outside. The result depends on mpp, not on the drawing. Separately, the float sums of widthM and Σown run in enumeration order and can flip a round6 tie under mirroring.
findings.failureScenario: Start from pierFront() in the D1 fixture (two 4 m mouths onto the open-plan house). Add a third interval past a WALL_RETURN at one end: a 2 m mouth into a 2 × 2.5 m porch closed on its other sides. Sweep the registration's mpp over 0.0490..0.0510 in 1e-5 steps. For part of the sweep the porch interval appears in `sharers` (its why reads 'one of 3 mouths…'), and the porch is BUILT. For the rest it stays OPEN_SIDE.
findings.proposedFix: Decide membership on cells, not m²: have pocketOf return the pocket bitmap. A gap is a sharer iff some cell of reachedShut(decided ∪ group∖g) ∖ reachedShut(decided ∪ group) is not in own(g)'s bitmap. Compute sharedM2 once from the shared cell set's px, summed in a fixed (iy, ix) order. Add an mpp-sweep and a mirror test for the three-interval fixture.

findings.title: The D1 joint limit is stricter than the merged span's and uncapped at 8 m; 'never shuts more than the incumbent did' is false
findings.claim: widthM is the sum of the sharers' interval widths. It excludes the separators' ink, the jamb re-cut and any non-sharer intervals, so limit(J) < limit(W_parent). Nothing caps J at maxWideOpeningM. Its own fixture shows the departure: pierFront's merged gap is 9 m, which the incumbent never weighs (OPEN_SIDE, 'where the wall stops'), and D1 shuts it. A shared space with 2.5·J² < S ≤ 2.5·W² is shut where the merged span left it open. With three 3 m mouths, J = 9 m is weighed although it is wider than any opening.
findings.failureScenario: Two 2.4 m mouths either side of a 0.3 m WALL_RETURN 1.5 m deep (W ≈ 5.1 m, J = 4.8 m) open onto one closed 5.1 × 11.8 m space (60 m²). D1: 60 > 57.6, so both are shut and BUILT. The incumbent merged gap: 60 < 65.0, so it stays open. The resolution's claim is contradicted.
findings.proposedFix: Either use the parent span's limit, max(6, 2.5·span.widthM²), and skip the group when span.widthM > maxWideOpeningM; this makes the claim true, but the D1 9 m fixture then becomes an explicit design decision. Or keep J, add `J ≤ maxWideOpeningM`, and correct resolution.md and architecture.md to say D1 can shut more than the incumbent.

findings.title: A completions-only override tags the outline-grid spans BOX: two BOX readings of one copy, and colliding pack event ids
findings.claim: decomposePlan stores compoundFacadesBoxReading whenever an override exists. boundaryExtension returns an override when anyAccepted OR completed.length > 0, but compoundFacadesOf labels the decomposition's own spans 'OUTLINE' only when boundary.accepted. With completions alone, both readings are emitted as 'BOX'. Span and interval ids are built from line and gap coordinates, so the outline grid's spans usually carry the same ids. The 12c timeline then gets duplicate objectIds `interval:<frame>/BOX/<id>`, possibly with different decisions, and the digest cannot say which reading built the model.

Better, carry `reading` on PlanDecomposition when decomposeCore runs with an override. Add a completions-only fixture asserting reading tags ['BOX', 'OUTLINE'] and unique event ids.

findings.title: Callout depth rule measures the touching wall piece only: a door or window in a garage's side or separator wall within 4.5 m refuses a real garage
findings.claim: left and right are inwardOf(returnRun(...)): the single solid piece touching the facade. returnRun's read window ends at 4.5 m + t, and openings (a door or window drawn with thin lines) break the solid layer. A garage whose separator wall has a door into the vestibule, or whose side wall has a door or window within 4.5 m of the front, has a run under 4.5 m and fails `left >= deeper && right >= deeper`. The blank garage with its own callout then falls to the pocket test (3 × 6.5 m = 19.5 < 22.5) and stays OPEN_SIDE. At 0e996b6 the threshold was max(0.9 m, 3t) and it was shut.
findings.failureScenario: Fixture 11 (entranceAndGarage({ garage: 'BLANK' }) with the 300 cm callout at the garage mouth) plus `p.clear(252, 200, 263, 215).line(257, 200, 257, 215)`: a door in the garage's right wall about 3 m in. Expected: OPENING_IN_WALL and builtAt(222, 210) true. Predicted: right ≈ 2.9 m < 4.5, role OPEN_SIDE, garage not built.
findings.proposedFix: Measure 'walls running on deeper than a recess' as the farthest wall-thick ink along that wall's line within the read window, allowing holes ≤ maxOpeningM, as backWallOf already allows holes. Do not use the length of the first piece. Add the side-door variant to fixture 11 and to M13.

findings.title: Pocket stage flood count roughly doubles, with redundant floods, and every flood rebuilds evidence-independent edge data
findings.claim: Floods per plan in the pocket stage go from 1+U (0e996b6) to 1+U+Σ_groups(1+|G|+[sharers≥2]). The bound is 24 spans × ≤ 9 intervals, so at most ≈ +260. Every pocketOf calls edgesFor, which recomputes wallIntervals and lineIntervals over the mask for every grid line although only `extra` changes. When |G| = 2, the leave-one-out floods equal the already-computed ownPocket of the other mouth. pocketOf(sharers) equals `all` when sharers == group, the common D1 case. Bounded, not a blow-up.
findings.failureScenario: A plan with 3 spans of 3 undecided intervals each needs 1 + 9 + 3·(1+3+1) = 25 floods instead of 10, and each one re-scans every grid line of the mask. On large sheets this is visible in the decomposePlan timing that is being measured.
findings.proposedFix: Precompute walls and drawn per grid line once and pass only `extra` into closureOf. Memoise pocketOf by a sorted key of gap extents (reuse ownPocket when |gs| = 1, and reuse `all` when sharers == group). Record the pocket-stage flood count in the perf harness.

verified.reasoning:
The mechanics in the claim are right, but what it calls a regression is the intended A2 fix, it is documented, and the claim's own fixture comes out better at HEAD than at the incumbent.

What the code does:
- At 0e996b6, plan-decomposition.ts reads the OPENING_IN_WALL gaps again inside the loop on every pass. The flood with everything open (`reachedOpen`) is taken once, before the loop. So once an earlier gap is shut, the cells behind it count in every later gap's pocket: they are reached in the open flood but not in the shut one.
- At HEAD (lines 2068-2088), `decided` is fixed before the test and every gap's own pocket is read before any decision is applied. That covers all undecided gaps, plain ones included.
- So yes: on a plan with no separator (unscaled ones included), a later plain gap no longer inherits an earlier one's pocket, and its decision can differ from 5957e3a.

Why this is not a defect:
1. **The change is intended and written down.**
   - architecture.md §3 says: "Every gap is weighed against the openings decided before the test and every own pocket is read before any decision is applied, so the result never follows the order lines are enumerated in (council A2)". That says every gap, not only compound intervals.
   - resolution.md, "Effect on the development rows", names the case outright. A plain 3.74 m gap on another line was shut first, and its pocket was counted again behind A05's compound mouths. The stage gives up that development gain on purpose.
   - The line "a gap with no accepted separator keeps the incumbent's decision exactly" (§2 / §3, council C2) is about compound children replacing their parent. It is not a promise to keep the incumbent's order-dependent loop. The claim itself concedes the incumbent was orientation-dependent, so it could not have been kept and A2 (rated P0) fixed at the same time. At most the two sentences in §3 read awkwardly side by side, which is a documentation nit.
2. **The claim's own fixture is right at HEAD.**
   - The hall behind the left-side gap is already shut on its own (37 m² against its 32.4 m² limit).
   - Counting it again behind the porch (12 + 37 = 49 > 40) is exactly the double count A2 removed. It turned a 12 m² porch, walled on three sides, into BUILT, which is a false closure.
   - HEAD keeps the porch open on its own 12 m², which is correct.
   - It is the same on unscaled plans, where only the double count disappears.
3. **The "real loss" (g stays open in front of a region R that it shares with a shut h) is not a regression in every case.**
   - For it to happen, one mouth h has to span two rooms: an exclusive pocket bigger than its limit, and R, split by a partition that ends at the mouth.
   - The incumbent caught it in only one enumeration order. When h is processed first, g's pocket is R plus h's own pocket counted a second time.
   - In the other order the incumbent did exactly what HEAD does now.
   - HEAD is the same in every orientation and no longer double counts. Missing R in that rare layout is a residual weakness (P2 at most). The monotone Jacobi rounds the claim proposes would improve it, but they are not needed to restore a contract.

What is left: a P3 wording nit in architecture.md §3, plus an optional P2 improvement (monotone Jacobi rounds). That falls short of the P1 the claim asserts.

The mechanism is real, but it cannot happen on a realistic plan, so this is not a P1.

What the claim gets right: at 0e996b6, compoundSpanOf returned null for no-room, no-ink and no-accepted-separator gaps. Only cut spans were pushed, so only they counted toward COMPOUND_BOUNDS.spans. After 65f0681, compound-facade.ts:377 `whole(...)` returns a span with `intervals: []`. plan-decomposition.ts:1495 pushes every non-null span, and :1494 checks `spans.length < COMPOUND_BOUNDS.spans` before calling compoundOf. compoundOf also runs before the maxWidePx check, so whole records now use up the 24-span budget, X lines first.

Why it does not happen in practice:
1. Only facade gaps count. facadeCompoundReader (plan-decomposition.ts:1570-1577) returns null without a span when the line is a set-back line, lies more than 1.5·wallPx from an envelope side, or falls outside the envelope's extent. Interior gaps use no budget.
2. A gap must be wider than maxOpeningM (3.2 m) and have two jambs of at least 0.5·wallPx.
3. thinLines (plan-decomposition.ts:562-578) merges grid lines closer than minCellM = 0.45 m. A wall's face and axis therefore end up on one line, and at most about two lines fall in the ±1.5-wall window. The "2-3 lines per opening" premise is mostly false.
4. The X-side facades of a house are two walls, typically 8-15 m each. Each can hold at most about 2-3 gaps over 3.2 m with jambs between them. That gives roughly 6 distinct gaps, or about 12 records with duplicates, well short of 24.

Reaching 24 needs about 12-24 separate wall-bounded gaps over 3.2 m on the two side facades alone. That is the failure fixture as stated, and it is a synthetic stress plan, not an unseen house.

Pre-existing limit: the 24-span cap was already order-dependent for cut spans at 0e996b6, a stated work bound (resolution E7 "bounded by COMPOUND_BOUNDS"). The fix only widens what counts toward an already order-dependent bound.

The core mechanism holds, but the failure scenario as written does not trigger it, so I rate it P2 rather than P1. I traced the code but did not run anything; the claim about how often it fires is reasoned from rounding arithmetic.

**The mechanism is real.** Sharer membership is decided at packages/reconstruction/src/plan-decomposition.ts:2096:
`all.m2 - pocketOf(group.filter(x => x !== g)).m2 > own(g)`

- `pocketOf` (2068-2081) sums cell px² in a fixed (iy, ix) order and returns `round6(px * mppArea)`. `round6` (source-common/src/geometry.ts:43) is `Math.round(v*1e6)/1e6`.
- Take a mouth g whose pocket P can only be reached through g. Then `shut(decided ∪ group∖g) \ shut(decided ∪ group)` and `own(g) = reachedOpen \ shut(decided ∪ {g})` are exactly the same set of cells: P. Shutting the other siblings does not change P, and the cells outside the envelope are pushed by construction.
- So in exact arithmetic the left side equals `own(g)`. In practice the code compares `round6(A·k) − round6(B·k)` with `round6((A−B)·k)`. With fractional parts in 1e-6 units of .6 and .4, the left side rounds to (A−B)+1e-6. The float subtraction of two round6 values also lands an ulp either side of the round6 literal. Grid px values can be non-integer (back-wall lines are added as round6 px, 1898), so A and B are inexact float sums.
- The test has zero tolerance, so it comes out true for a noticeable share of mpp values (roughly 1/8 or more under uniform fractional parts). That share depends on the registration's mpp, not on the drawing.
- Once g is wrongly in `sharers` (with two genuine sharers in the same span), `sharedM2` is still about the shared interior, because own(g) cancels. But `widthM` grows by w_g, so the limit 2.5·W² moves. For pierFront it goes from 160 m² to 302.5 m² with a 3 m third mouth. Two outcomes follow:
  - If the interior is between 160 and 302.5 m², it is no longer shut: the D1 false opening comes back.
  - If the interior is above 302.5 m², g is shut with the other two even though its own pocket alone stays under its own limit (a false closure).

**The proposed scenario does not reach that code path.** A 2 m mouth into a 2 × 2.5 m porch "closed on its other sides" has returns at both ends and a back wall within RECESS_MAX_DEPTH_M = 4.5 m. compound-facade.ts:429/457 makes it RECESS_MOUTH, and line 2093 excludes RECESS_MOUTH from `siblings`. That porch is never weighed as a sharer.

A g that does trigger it must be OPEN_SIDE, no wider than maxWideOpeningM, have a nonempty isolated pocket, and sit in the same compound span as the two sharers. That means either a pocket deeper than 4.5 m (for example a garage with no door drawn) or one whose returns or back wall were not read.

**Secondary claim is weak.** The orientation dependence via the summation order of `widthM` / Σown only matters at an exact float tie of `sharedM2 <= limitM2`. That is a P3 nit at most.

**Gating conditions.** The defect needs three or more non-recess intervals in one span, two of them sharing an interior, and a third leading to an isolated non-recess pocket. That is generic in mechanism but narrow in configuration, hence P2.

**Smallest fix:** decide membership on exact cell counts rather than m². The cell sets are identical in the isolated case, and integer counts are exact: `all.cells - pocketOf(group.filter(x => x !== g)).cells > (ownPocket.get(g)?.cells ?? 0)`. The alternative is to keep m² and require a margin of at least one cell's area.
